title: The Qualitative Laboratory: Theory Prototyping and Hypothesis Generation with Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2601.00797v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The use of Large Language Models (LLMs) to simulate social actors has garnered attention for its implications for the epistemic status of discourses generated through such means. This paper considers the more modest question of whether sociological role-playing can serve as a heuristic instrument in the generation of qualitative hypotheses. We take as a case study the development of four divergent fictional characters using a theoretically informed Matrix of Climate Reception. These characters are asked to respond to a series of discourse frames covering two topics: a proposed ban on the sale of new gasoline-powered cars, and the inclusion of climate justice in the school curriculum. We then analyse the 32 model-generated responses for their commonalities, situational differences and divergences from the presuppositions underlying the characters' profiles. translated_title: 定性实验室：基于大语言模型的理论原型构建与假设生成
translated_abstract: 使用大语言模型（LLM）模拟社会行动者的做法，因其对由此生成的言论的认识论地位所产生的影响而受到关注。本文则考虑一个更为审慎的问题：社会学角色扮演能否作为一种启发性工具，用于定性假设的生成。我们以利用基于理论的“气候接受矩阵”（Matrix of Climate Reception）构建四个立场迥异的虚构角色作为案例研究。这些角色被要求对一系列话语框架作出回应，涵盖两个议题：一项关于禁止销售新型燃油汽车的提案，以及将气候正义纳入学校课程。随后，我们分析了32个模型生成的回应，考察其中的共性、情境差异，以及与角色设定中潜在预设的分歧。该实验展示了如何利用大语言模型来充实理论……
tldr: 本文通过构建四个虚构角色回应燃油车禁令与气候正义教育相关话语框架的实验，展示了大语言模型可以作为社会学定性研究中构建理论原型和生成假设的启发性工具。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates, through an experiment with four fictional characters responding to climate-related discourse frames, that LLM-based sociological role-playing can serve as a heuristic tool for theory prototyping and qualitative hypothesis generation.
